tts: You live on the tenth floor, and you're tired of hauling groceries up the stairs.
So you put a wheel on the roof, throw a rope over it, and tie on a box. Pull, and the box goes up. But with you inside, it weighs a couple hundred pounds.
So on the other end of the rope, you hang a weight that's almost as heavy: a counterweight. Now they balance each other, and moving the box is easy.
Pulling is still a chore, so you put a motor at the top to turn the wheel. And so the box doesn't swing, you run it on rails inside a shaft.
But if the rope snaps, the box falls. So you add a spring with teeth: while the rope is tight, it stays tucked in. If the rope breaks, the teeth bite into the rails, and the box stops.
And so nobody steps into an empty shaft, the doors on each floor only open when the box is there.
Finally, you add buttons, so the motor knows where to stop.
Congrats, you just invented the elevator. And that safety brake? In eighteen fifty-four, Elisha Otis showed it off by having his own rope cut in front of a crowd. He didn't fall.
